notes.content:
Hey everyone!! New update is now live!

Change log:
- New Map (not too pretty, but ... it's something :P )
- Steam Matchmaking
- Auto-Portforward (UPnP)
- New weapons
- New weapon sounds

This is still far away from being called a "game" but I have very little time to work on this more than I already do, sorry.

Hope you can have some fun with your friends ;)


P.S: UPnP should work with around 90% of todays routers. If your router doesn't support UPnP, then please check portforward.com website for instructions on how to open ports.
Ports for the game are TCP & UDP 7777.

notes.title: Future of the Game and Release date
notes.content:
Hello everyone :)

The game will have a future :)

Steam P2P networking system failed, you can see my testing here: https://youtu.be/W_saZWNSlVA
As you can see... Steam P2P is not made for real time (it never was, I just decided to try it out since it was free).

Now what? Well I will continue to work on the game like previously was. I will build on top of what's made (the networking part is all made) but it uses Listen servers, a.k.a Player hosted servers. 
I will develop a NAT punchthrough application that will auto-portforward your router to allow networking to be made through your PC.
This is not mandatory, but it's essential if you are planning to host a lobby/server/match.
Also, you should be asking yourself why didn't I try this at first, well the thing is, some routers (about 10% I believe) don't support Port-forwarding, even if they do, some ISP's block this, and that NAT punchthrough application may not work at all on some routers, and that excludes some people from creating lobbies. That's why I was going to use Steam P2P which uses Steam relay servers to send messages and thus no need to portforward :)

I'll keep on trying for the release date of the end of the month, and I think I can have the FPS and TPS models ready, animated and working weapon selling machines by that time. 

Thank you again for all your support.

notes.title: Bad news about Networking
notes.content:
It was with some discontent that today I checked the results after testing the Steam P2P networking approach.
For those who don't know what this was, it's basically how the game would play out in terms of networking, all data (player movements, shootings, etc) would be exchanged through Steam servers, player to player (peer-to-peer). 

So, the news. At first I was head first, implemented the full FPS controllers, shooting and all that and tested how movement, shooting, look-around would be sent through the internet to connected players. It didn't go well. The movements were very jerky and delayed but I decided to scale it down. 

After that fail, I scaled down to a 2D test. A cube, with X,Y movement and have it send [b]ONLY[/b] that information. It didn't go well either. I would move the cube in one pc, and the other pc didn't receive anything, but passing some time (around 20-30seconds) there was a bit of movement but, again, jerky and (super) delayed.

I guess this was expected, as Steam doesn't want full games relying on their servers, but at least I had to try.

So, this leaves two options which I will think over and over, do yet some more testing to see if I can go around some things.

Option #1: Give up. It's hard, not only for me, that I have a 10 page document with lots of information about what would be this game, and the amount of assets I produced and gathered, but for the people that supported me, with feedback and kind words.

Option #2: Go with Listen Servers. For those that don't know, Listen Servers is a way of saying Dedicated Servers that are player hosted. This is an approach used for example by CoD games (remmember Host Migration?) and it's actually a good approach, but with a down side : Port Forwarding.
If you want others to join your server/game, you would need to Port Forward which is a thing that some people either don't know how to do, or can't because ISP's block that functionality in the routers. With this method, those people wouldn't be allowed to play the game with their friends or other people from around the world, and that's also hard for me to do. I've had that problem with AffordaGolf and it was not pleasant.

These are the options, of course, giving up is easier, but I'm still not sold on that. I'll continue testing, and I'll research on NAT punchthrough. NAT Punchthrough can be the key to make this game playable for everyone. It makes auto-portfowarding as easy as pressing a button.


I want to say again, I'm sorry to those who supported and believed in this project, I will keep you updated.

notes.title: Devblog Update - Animations, Network and Map Editor
notes.content:
Today I don't have any fancy prints for you due to me working on some behind the scenes stuff.

[h1]Animations[/h1]
I'm currently working with First-Person animations, such as Idle, Reload, Fire, ADS etc but I'm not a very good animator, so it will take some more time.

[h1]Network[/h1]
I also started the Full Network System, which consists of Matchmaking + Lobbies + P2P.

I can't really continue working on this because Valve blocked the Lobby Creation for F2P games, and I've asked them to enable it so I can test it, but I think it will work.
If it doesn't work like expected, I will have to do a Client-Server approach using a Listen Server (One player is the host/server while playing). This is the last resort since it needs portforwarding to work in some cases, and that's a pain in the butt to do.

Meanwhile I'll continue working on the map and guns.

[h1]Map Editor[/h1]
I've researched on some map editors for various games, and I decided that the best option is to make a "tile" based map editor. There will be tiles with some pre-determined sizes, (1x1, 2x2, 5x5, 10x10) and variants, for floors and walls. Then you can choose from a library of textures to apply to those tiles to create your map.

I have around 1500 textures (including bump and normal maps) ready to be used by you, and I hope this comes in handy for the creative ones :)

Thank you for your support, my hand is better and at least I can type well with it.

notes.title: Devblog Update #5 - Game Modes
notes.content:
Zombie games can get dull sometimes, so why not add some game modes to change airs for a bit?

So I've received some good feedback on additional game modes that are as follows: 

[list]
    [*]Round Based Survival
The classic endless waves, try to hold on the longer you can.

    [*]Protect the VIP
Same as Round based Survival, but this time you and your team mates have the mission to not only survive, but to protect a VIP. This VIP sometimes gets a little scared, and runs away from your team (and from zombies) but can get in trouble and you and your team mates must follow and protect him/her.
    
[*] Rescue
Some NPC's are stuck somewhere. You and your team mates must go there, rescue them and bring them home.

[*]Base defense
Protect a small base from endless waves of enemies. This differs from Round Based Survival in terms o Map. The maps in RBS will be divided into sections and can be open. In Base defense, you are stuck in a division of the map and zombies come to you from all sides.
[/list]

These are still on paper, but I think they promise good and fun hours of gameplay. 

As always, what's your opinion? Your feedback matters!

Thank you for your messages of support.

notes.title: Devblog Update #4 - Customization
notes.content:
Hi everyone, today we'll talk about customization.

This will be key part in the game, as it's important to everyone to play like they want and to look like they want. 
In the game it will be possible to customize Weapons and Chracters.

[h1]Weapon Customization[/h1]
Weapon customization will be based on skins. Skins can be bought and sold in the Steam Community Market and are awarded at matches end as well as War Packs.

[h1]Character Customization[/h1]
Character customization will be based on clothes and equipment that players can equip for cosmetic only. Items are won by opening War Packs awarded at the end of matches at random. 

[h1]Item rarity[/h1]
Each customization item has a rarity associated with a degrees scale.
[list]

[*]1st Degree - Common
[*]2nd Degree - Uncommon
[*]3rd Degree - Rare
[*]4th Degree - Very Rare
[*]5th Degree - Legendary
[*]6th Degree - Epic
[*]7th Degree - Special
[/list]

Every skin will be possible to win with in-game time.

As always, I'm open to suggestions :)
Thank you for your support.

[*]1st Degree - Common
[*]2nd Degree - Uncommon
[*]3rd Degree - Rare
[*]4th Degree - Very Rare
[*]5th Degree - Legendary
[*]6th Degree - Epic
[*]7th Degree - Special
[/list]

Every skin will be possible to win with in-game time.

As always, I'm open to suggestions :)
Thank you for your support.

notes.title: Devblog Update #2 - Classes
notes.content:
[h1]Players can choose a class in the lobby to have some advantages. Each class has an Active and a Passive skill. [/h1]
Active Skill is a meter that is filled over time (slowly) and for each kill it fills a specific amount.


[list]
    [*]Scout
- Can become invisible to zombies for a period of time (fillable meter)
- Walks 20% faster.

    [*]Hunter
- Can place traps (fillable meter)
- 70% discount on map traps

    [*]Tank
- Can become invincible for a period of time (fillable meter)
- 70% more health

    [*]Assault
- Can instant kill for a period of time (fillable meter)
- 20% more damage

    [*]Medic
- Heal everyone in team (fillable meter)
- 70% discount on health packs

    [*]Support
- Team Max Ammo (fillable meter)
- 70% discount on ammo packs
[/list]

These stats are not final, and are yet subjective to testing and balancing.

Thanks for your support.
If you have anything to add, please do.

notes.title: The future of this Demo
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I wanted to say one thing or two about the future of this Demo.
It started out as as the name says, a Demo for a tutorial series which I made on How to create a Multiplayer FPS. 

Then, some of you got it and made fun of it, which is totally fine, some of you didn't get it and made fun also, which again, it's fine. But what is not fine is assumptions on my work and most of all false assumptions. 

But after some thought, I now see an opportunity to make something good out of this. Many people contacted me interested in the future of this game, and I told them that this was just a Demo and wouldn't be developed any further. Well that might not be the case.

I have an idea, and I'd like to know if anyone would be interested in that.

The idea is to turn this into a full game. What I mean is that I will continue developing the game and improve not only the looks (graphics) but also game mechanics and turn this game into a good old zombies game. 
My favourite zombie survival game was Black Ops 2's Zombies (thus me doing the Kino-clone map) and [b]I would like to know if it's on your interest to have a free-to-play "clone" (new maps, weapons and gameplay features ofc) of that Call of Duty mode.[/b]

You may be wondering what new features? 
Well I don't really now yet, and I'm open to suggestions. What I do know is that I'll try to use the Steam inventory system and Steam market for customization items because I believe customization is key for a good game. You will be able to make your own weapon and clothing skins, and trade them in the inventory.
Also, if you don't like the genre of Call of Duty's Zombies mode, you can suggest other, except open world like DayZ because that's just way to hard do on my own.

Thank  you all for your feedback, I've read every review and every thread. I'm gonna try to not let you down!

A few foot notes:
[list]
    [*]I'm a software engineer. A programmer. I'm not an artist, but I know my way into 3D low poly modelling. So that's the look I'm going with. Not minecraft low poly, but not AAA high-poly either. So.. in the middle probably.
    [*]I'll be doing this alone in this month of August in my free time.
    [*]I'll try to be active on the discussions, everything you wanna ask, ask there please.
[*]Also suggestions... please give your feedback and suggestions, anything really.
[/list]

notes.title: A note about this Demo.
notes.content:
I've seen two reviews that show that this store page is not as clear as it should be.

Let me explain: This is a working multiplayer FPS. By working I mean, you can host your own server, and have people join it (by sharing your IP address). There you can kill (2) zombies or other players, pickup weapons, health and walk around the map.

But this isn't a full game. This is just the build of what YOU (yes you) can create by watching the video series "How to Create a Multiplayer FPS" linked in the description. 

Finally, let me put it in this way: This only shows the gameplay you can create on your own (by watching the videos that explain everything), and with some other models, menus, sounds, and those "details", you can have your own Multiplayer FPS up and running :) 

Hope you enjoy this demo, and if you decide to check the series, hope you enjoy them as well.

Any questions just ask on the discussion forums :)

Kind regards,
Vitor.
